IEE Colloquium on Oversampling Techniques and Sigma-Delta Modulation
abstract: The advantages and disadvantages of L>or=1 sigma-delta modulators are given. Nonidealities including multibit quantisation, error correction and loop delay are considered. Performance parameters, evaluation and simulation are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Use of clipping in sigma-delta modulators
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling Techniques and Sigma-Delta Modulation
abstract: High-resolution conversion processes utilising sigma-delta modulation (SDM) with practical sampling rates and single-bit quantisers require high-order loop filters. Third- and higher-order systems are particularly prone to instability when the input signal approaches full-scale (set by the quantiser output voltage), and such overload instability results in very low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) observed at the modulator output. This paper shows by simulation how this type of instability in a fourth-order coder can be avoided by placing clippers at loop-filter integrator outputs, and how optimal choice of clipper levels can increase the SNR observed when the modulator is in overload, from less than 0 dB without clippers to 40 dB->80 dB. Results generated using clippers where integrator outputs are reset are compared with those of saturating clippers. Other techniques for avoiding overload instability, such as adaptive loop filters, are also considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital signal processing on a sigma-delta bitstream
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling Techniques and Sigma-Delta Modulation
abstract: This paper presents a third-order modulator designed giving 16-bit resolution at 64 times oversampling without multi-bit multiplies. Consideration is given to two filter examples in the context of a single-chip analogue I/O filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling Techniques and Sigma-Delta Modulation
abstract: By incorporating the principle of a closed loop transducer with the over sampled converter the authors obtain a directly digital device having the properties of linear transfer characteristic, frequency response down to DC, self-testing properties and accuracy-to-bandwidth trade off. Prototype transducers have been built and tested.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed signal acquisition systems for sonar applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling Techniques and Sigma-Delta Modulation
abstract: The authors demonstrate that compact low-cost low-power sonar signal acquisition systems with wide dynamic range have been produced routinely using noise-shaping convertors implemented in hybrid thick-film and surface mount technologies. They outline convertor topologies exploiting the available passive component matching. Digital circuitry has been fabricated using custom ASIC technology. High-performance multichannel systems can be assembled for various applications ranging from a few hundred Hz (narrowband towed array systems) to 100 kHz (mine hunting).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Phase correction techniques for bandpass sigma delta A-D converters
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling Techniques and Sigma-Delta Modulation
abstract: This paper demonstrates the use of phase corrective filtering techniques in such converters implemented with continuous time filters. The third order converter described employs a novel overload recovery mechanism which introduces minimal switching noise to the output, and has considerable performance advantages compared with those employing overload detect/reset circuitry.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A flexible decimation filter architecture for sigma-delta converters
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling Techniques and Sigma-Delta Modulation
abstract: The authors' objective is to design an architecture for the implementation of a general polyphase recursive all-pass filter sharing common functional blocks and minimizing the use of storage, which can process a sample in one clock cycle. The architecture should be self-sufficient to realize a chain of cascaded decimation filters which attenuates out-of-band noise and decimates the signal to the lowest sampling rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Issues in the design of low oversampling ratio single bit sigma-delta modulators
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling Techniques and Sigma-Delta Modulation
abstract: The linear delta modulator is shown to be a special instance of the more general sigma-delta modulator, in which the signal and noise transfer functions are equal. High order sigma-delta systems may be designed which retain the single pole -6 dB/octave overloading characteristics, but with the advantages of higher order noise shaping. Techniques for adaptive step size, both instantaneous and syllabic may be adopted to give companding operation. With slight damping of the loop integrators, the cutoff phenomenon may be used to give a noise gating effect. These techniques have been used for a design study for the integration of a switched capacitor speech coder/decoder with a bit rate of 32 to 64 kbits/s. The resulting system gives a significant performance improvement with similar complexity compared with a linear pulse code (PCM) approach using the same bit rate. In this application, there is no requirement for digital decimators and interpolators to process the digital data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Switched current circuit design techniques for single-bit, high speed sigma-delta modulators
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling Techniques and Sigma-Delta Modulation
abstract: This paper reviews some research aimed at developing suitable circuit techniques to implement high speed Sigma Delta modulators on a pure digital process technology. Techniques are presented in both Si and GaAs technologies, and in both instances performance is optimised for speed. Simulations presented for the Si circuits employ MOSFETs from the 0.8 mu m Northern Telecom BiCMOS technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the configuration of second order sigma delta modulator
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling Techniques and Sigma-Delta Modulation
abstract: A set of differential equations has been constructed to represent a continuous sigma delta modulator. This paper is concerned with an analysis of these equations, with particular reference to values representing the gains of the feedback loop and the integrator leakage. The results are presented in the form of stability plots. Conditions for the stability of the equations representing second order modulation are derived. The results are used on a conventional simulation of sigma-delta modulation, and the applicability of this method is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
